function: Over-the-air (AirComp) aggregation of LoRA updates in federated fine-tuning of a text-to-image diffusion model, with energy-minimizing bandwidth, power, GPU frequency, and denoising-factor allocation (p. 1, p. 5).
system: Single-antenna UGVs to a single-antenna UAV parameter server at 100 m over A2G links (scalar channels); no RIS; 2 GHz carrier, 5 MHz bandwidth (p. 5, p. 12).
method: Federated (FedAvg) DreamBooth-LoRA fine-tuning of text-to-image diffusion models (SD v1-5 mainly) aggregated by AirComp; resources set by non-learned block coordinate descent (p. 5, p. 11, p. 13).
data_channel: Custom simulator: block fading AirComp uplink, A2G LoS/NLoS path loss for the UAV downlink; fine-tuning images from a disaster image dataset and Unsplash (p. 5, p. 6, p. 11).
test_conditions: 3-5 images per UGV, 100 rounds of 10 local iterations; energy evaluated versus number of UGVs (3-11), latency deadline, and MSE threshold (p. 11, p. 14, p. 15).
baselines: Base model, traditional full fine-tuning [10], proposed without AirComp (OFDMA); resource allocation: SGHS-RA heuristic [22], water-filling power [12], equal computing [40], equal bandwidth allocation (p. 12, p. 14).
metrics: CLIP score, BRISQUE, total system energy consumption, local uploading energy, optimal denoising factor, and BCD convergence (p. 13, p. 14, p. 15).
complexity: BCD resource allocation complexity O(I(m1 + m2 n r + m3 log2 F) c_max); LoRA reduces per-round upload from 3.2 GB to 3.07 MB (p. 11, p. 14).
q1_support: p. 5: "We consider a frequency nonselective block fading channel model"; p. 6: A2G path loss "can be modeled as [33]". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 11: "We perform 100 global rounds, with each global round comprising 10 local fine-tuning iterations." The fine-tuned model is evaluated only in its training setting; the sweeps over UGV number, latency, and MSE threshold (pp. 14-15) rerun the optimization, not a test in unseen conditions.
q3_support: p. 14: "Self-adaptive global best harmony search-based resource allocation (SGHS-RA) [22]: It is a heuristic method"; p. 12: "this scheme uses OFDMA instead of AirComp". Non-learned allocation baselines exist, but no earlier published over-the-air aggregation design is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the proposed algorithm has a complexity of O(I (m1 + m2 nr + m3 log2 (F ))cmax ) in total" (cost of the BCD resource and denoising-factor design).
q5_support: p. 11: "mainly sourced from the disaster image dataset [41] or Unsplash". Only public images of the learning task; channels are simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: Include. Federated learning over the air passes the learning check: LoRA updates are aggregated by AirComp (p. 5: "We consider the FedAvg for federated aggregation and utilize the AirComp technology"); the resource allocation itself is non-learned BCD (p. 11). The AirComp links are single-antenna with no RIS (p. 5, scalar h_i,t), but the parameter server is a UAV over A2G links (p. 3, p. 5), so I read it as an NTN (aerial) work that admits single-antenna links; if the reviewer limits that exception to area 6 works, the decision becomes exclude, system, p. 5. Area 7 rather than 6 because the paper designs the over-the-air aggregation itself (closed-form denoising factor under an AirComp MSE threshold, p. 10) and 7 is more specific. q3: Traditional [10] differs only in fine-tuning all parameters, WFPA [12] sets the UAV downlink power (p. 8, p. 14), and SGHS-RA [22] is a heuristic, so none is an earlier over-the-air aggregation design; non-learned comparisons are on energy (Fig. 7, p. 14).
